lines: It kept me standing. Crops recover faster when the farmer does too.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
The new scratches tell me it took more than one hard blow.
That dent sits where the armor turned a strike away from my ribs.
I felt the shield catch before I understood what had swung at me.
One strap loosened during the fight. It needs fixing before I wear it again.
The weight bothered me at first, then the fighting started and I forgot it.
I am alive to complain about the fit, so it served me well.
Mud worked into every buckle, but nothing important gave way.
The helmet rang like a bell when something hit it.
I trusted the gear more after the first strike failed to break through.
The padding is torn where I fell. The outer layer held.
I could move well enough to reach cover when it mattered.
There is blood on it, but less than there might have been.
I would wear the same set again after a careful repair.
The shield edge is chipped from keeping trouble away from my face.
It bought me the moment I needed to get back on my feet.
Check the fastenings. I pulled them hard while I was running.
Whatever happened out there, the gear carried its share of the fight.
Unused, thankfully. I would rather wear out a hoe than armor.
Nothing reached me closely enough to test it. That suits me fine.
The gear came home cleaner than my boots.
I kept it ready, but the danger never found us.
The shield stayed on my back for the whole journey.
I practiced drawing it, though I never had to block a strike.
Every strap is still where you set it.
I am glad I carried the weight and never needed the protection.
It felt awkward on the first mile and natural by the last.
No dents, no cuts, and no story worth boasting about.
I checked the buckles each morning in case that quiet day changed.
The helmet stayed packed once we knew the road was clear.
I would still adjust the shoulder before another long trip.
The padding stayed dry, which feels like an achievement after that rain.
I learned how to move in it without learning how it handles a blow.
Peace kept the metal bright. I hope it does so again.
The gear was ready before I was, but neither of us saw combat.
I carried it because safety is never promised at the gate.
Let us inspect it anyway. An unused strap can still crack.
I brought every piece back untouched, and I am grateful for that.
